wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for tomato ketchup: tomatoes cooked with onions, spiced 5% cider vinegar, sugar and salt, reduced by half, hot packed in pint jars and processed in a boiling-water bath.

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: The FDA list gives tomatoes a pH of about 4.30–4.90, so some tomatoes have a pH slightly above 4.6.
Tomatoes canned as an acid food must be acidified to pH 4.6 or lower.
Do not use tomatoes from dead or frost-killed vines.

This recipe gets its acid only from the vinegar (most mixtures of low-acid and acid foods have a pH above 4.6 unless the recipe includes enough lemon juice, citric acid or vinegar); do not alter the vinegar, food or water proportions and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not change the amounts of the acid ingredients or of the fruit and vegetables; the recipe is tested only in the proportions given.
White distilled vinegar and cider vinegar of 5% acidity are recommended for pickles.
Penn State Extension advises vinegar of 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and advises against diluting vinegar with water unless a research-tested recipe says so.

JarAtlas rule (cautious, for readers outside the USA): use white distilled (spirit) vinegar or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity; do not use 10% vinegar and do not dilute it with water to make 5% vinegar; add only the water the recipe lists.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.

For 6 to 7 pint jars NCHFP lists 24 pounds (about 10.9 kg) of ripe tomatoes, 3 cups of chopped onions, 3/4 teaspoon of ground red pepper (cayenne), 3 cups of cider vinegar (5%), 4 teaspoons of whole cloves, 3 crushed cinnamon sticks, 1 1/2 teaspoons of whole allspice, 3 tablespoons of celery seeds, 1 1/2 cups of sugar and 1/4 cup of salt.
Wash the tomatoes, dip them in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds or until the skins split, then dip them in cold water.
Slip off the skins, remove the cores and quarter the tomatoes into a 4-gallon (about 15 l) stockpot or a large kettle.
Add the onions and red pepper, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Cover, turn off the heat and let stand for 20 minutes.
Put the spices in a spice bag, add it to the vinegar in a 2-quart (about 1.9 l) saucepan and bring to a boil.
Remove the spice bag, combine the vinegar with the tomato mixture and boil for about 30 minutes.
Put the boiled mixture through a food mill or sieve and return it to the pot.
Add the sugar and salt and boil gently, stirring often, until the volume is reduced by half or until the mixture rounds up on a spoon without separating.
Fill the hot pint jars, leaving 1/8 inch (about 0.3 cm) of headspace.
Remove air bubbles and adjust the headspace if needed.
Wipe the jar rims with a damp clean paper towel, put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 15 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 20 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 25 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
The NCHFP table gives times only for pint jars.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml.
